title: Finite constructibility under canonical quotient realization
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite, W a scheme, n≥0 and P=PbcQuotient(pbcIntegralDatum l E,n). If a fixed P-module sheaf F is intrinsically constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], then pbcFunctionRealization(W,d,n)(F) [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], restricted along pbcLevelConstantComparison(W,d,n), is an intrinsically constructible coefficient-module sheaf over the constant ring sheaf P_W. The coefficient inverse images and all finite local models are the actual ones of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. This includes empty schemes and imposes no etale-origin hypothesis.

source.place: Module sheafification and constant modules, Tags 03CY and 03DA; proetale.tex, finite local models and constructibility Tags 09AJ and 099Y.

proof.text: Use the fixed-scalar restriction and constant-comparison constructions from the generic constant-module encoding. The module-sheafification unit identifies every fixed sheaf with the encoding of its quotient realization. Normalize the quotient scalar map as in lem-sbc-finite-witness-realization. Restricting along the constant-to-function comparison then identifies the encoding with F itself.

For each stratum immersion, transport the fixed-scalar upper-star/lower-star adjunction across the scalar-encoding equivalences. The direct-image comparison is the identity on sections; the sheafification adjunction proves its scalar square. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the actual coefficient inverse image encoding with fixed inverse image. In particular inverse images of constant modules encode as constant fixed-module sheaves.

Keep the given finite positive constructible stratification. On each stratum, finite_models_of_fixed_lisse gives finite constant models. Convert to slice models using finiteModels_over. Pull their covering sieve back to the chosen terminal object. On each member restrict the model isomorphism to the smaller slice. The encoding is fully faithful there, so lift the isomorphism to the actual inverse-image module sheaf. These same finite models establish relative finite lissity on every stratum.

lean.statement:
theorem sbcFiniteRealization_constructible (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (W : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (ProEt.topology W)
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ProEtale.PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n)))
    (hF : IsConstructibleProEtaleFixedModuleSheaf W
      (ProEtale.PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n) F) :
    IsConstructibleProEtaleCoefficientModuleSheaf W
      (ProEtale.PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n)
      ((pbcRestrict (pbcLevelConstantComparison W (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).hom).obj
        ((pbcFunctionRealization W (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).obj F))
